newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ferrero looks for 8 trln lire sales in '96.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ferrero looks for 8 trln lire sales in '96.

text.p: One of Italy's largest food groups, the privately-owned Ferrero, expects to top eight trillion lire of sales in 1996, in its 50th year of trading, Italian newspapers reported on Sunday.

The group with brands like Nutella chocolate spread, Rocher and Ferrero chocolate brands, and Tic Tac sweets is one of Italy's top three food group along with Barilla, also privately-owned, and the quoted company Parmalat.
Ferrero is clearly Italy's leading confectionery group, but lags behind other groups such a Nestle SA, Mars and Cadbury Schweppes Plc in the whole of Europe.
The financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said that 1996 will result in group sales of almost eight trillion lire compared to some 7.327 trillion lire recorded in 1995.
The paper said that under the chairmanship of Michele Ferrero, son of the founder of the company, the group had expanded to employ 14,000 people, of which 6,500 were in Italy.
The group has continued to push up investment which amounted to 600 billion lire in the last five years in Italy, where the group has five factories.

But for 1996, a majority of its group sales will coming from outside its homeland with ex-Italy sales amounting to around five trillion lire compared to three trillion lire seen in Italy, which compares to 2.847 trillion lire Italian sales in 1995.
Looking outside continental Euorpe, in Ferrero's "Overseas 2000" plan, the group aims to gain two trillion lire of sales by the year 2000 from areas outside the European Union.
Ferrero already has factories in Australia, Puerto Rico, the United States, Ecuador and Argentina and is presently constructing a new factory in Brazil,
